smtp.title: SMTP
smtp.intro: Send emails using SMTP instead of the REST API.
smtp.subtitle: Point your app's SMTP client at this deployment's relay.
smtp.passwordNote: Use any API key as the password.
smtp.passwordTooltip: The relay authenticates with any of your API keys — paste one in place of YOUR_API_KEY. Keys are never shown here.
smtp.tlsWarnTitle: The SMTP relay is not running
smtp.tlsWarnBody: This deployment has no TLS certificate for the relay, so the smtp service refuses to start and keeps restarting. Set SMTP_TLS_CERT_PATH and SMTP_TLS_KEY_PATH, or enable SMTP_ALLOW_INSECURE_AUTH only on a private, trusted network.
smtp.insecureNote: TLS is not configured and SMTP_ALLOW_INSECURE_AUTH is on: clients authenticate without encryption. Set SMTP_TLS_CERT_PATH and SMTP_TLS_KEY_PATH to require STARTTLS.

unsubscribe.title: Unsubscribe page
unsubscribe.subtitle: Customize the hosted page recipients see when they unsubscribe.
unsubscribe.successMessagePlaceholder: Shown after someone unsubscribes or saves their preferences.
unsubscribe.showLogoNote: Your team logo replaces the MillionSend wordmark at the top of the page.
unsubscribe.showLogoMissing: Upload a team logo in the Settings tab to enable this.
unsubscribe.redirectUrlNote: Where to send recipients after they unsubscribe. Leave blank to keep them on the confirmation page.

ses.title: Connect your AWS SES
ses.subtitle: Your instance sends through your own SES account.

setup.cliNote: Run it anywhere Node 18+ and YOUR AWS admin credentials live — your laptop or the server. It creates everything and prints the .env lines to paste if MillionSend runs elsewhere.
setup.scriptNote: Paste into a terminal where the AWS CLI has admin credentials. It creates the IAM user, policy, SNS topic, and configuration set, then prints your .env lines.
setup.eventsSkipped: APP_BASE_URL is not a public https URL, so the event ingestion part is left out. Set it and reload to include it.
setup.cfnNote: One click: opens the CloudFormation review page with the hosted template — the same stack as infra/millionsend-ses.cfn.yaml. From a terminal instead:
setup.step1: Create a policy: IAM console → Policies → Create policy → JSON — paste this document.
setup.step2: Create a user named millionsend and attach the policy.
setup.step3: Create an access key for the user and paste it into .env.
setup.step4: Optional events: SNS topic + configuration set — the script above automates this part; see SELF_HOSTING.md.

credentials.title: Credentials
credentials.keysChain: not set — the default provider chain will be attempted
credentials.snsNote: not set — event ingestion is disabled
credentials.configSetNote: not set — SES publishes no events
credentials.authEmailNote: not set — password recovery is hidden

test.title: Test connection
test.note: runs GetAccount from the instance — read-only, nothing is sent
test.sandboxTitle: Your SES account is in sandbox.
test.sandboxBody: Recipients must be verified until AWS grants production access.
test.requestTemplate:
Use case: transactional email (account notifications, receipts, password resets) sent through MillionSend, a self-hosted sending platform we operate on our own infrastructure.

Recipients: our own users. List subscriptions follow double-opt-in guidance before any sending.

Bounce and complaint handling: SES delivery events are ingested via SNS; hard bounces and complaints are suppressed automatically and are never mailed again.

Expected volume: [VOLUME] emails/day, ramping up gradually.
test.requestTemplateNote: Replace [VOLUME], then paste it into the AWS production access request form.
test.rateHint: SES_MAX_SEND_RATE={envRate} in .env · account max {accountRate}/s — these disagree.

errors.credentials: AWS rejected the credentials — check AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in .env.
errors.unreachable: SES did not respond — check AWS_REGION and the network path.

next.title: Next steps

mcp.title: MCP server
mcp.intro: Let AI agents send email and manage your audience over the Model Context Protocol.
mcp.subtitle: Every tool call goes through the same rules as the REST API: verified domains, suppressions, quotas and team scoping.
mcp.serverUrlNote: Streamable HTTP endpoint. Clients sign in with your MillionSend account through OAuth — no API keys and nothing secret to paste.

notes.claudeCode: Then run /mcp inside Claude Code and pick millionsend to sign in.
notes.claudeDesktop: Add to claude_desktop_config.json — or skip the file: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector, and paste the server URL.
notes.cursor: Save as .cursor/mcp.json in the project, or ~/.cursor/mcp.json for every project.
notes.vscode: Save as .vscode/mcp.json in the workspace, then start the server from the editor's MCP view.

mcp.authNote: On first connect the browser opens a consent screen where you pick the team and permissions the client gets. The grant appears under <link>Connected apps</link>, where any member can revoke it.
mcp.toolsIntro: A client only sees the tools its granted permissions cover.

connectedApps.title: Connected apps
connectedApps.intro: Apps and MCP clients authorized through OAuth to act on this team.
connectedApps.empty: No apps connected yet. Authorize an MCP client and its grant appears here.
connectedApps.revokeAllTeamsForbidden: This grant also covers teams you do not administer. Only its holder can revoke it.

revokeConfirm.title: Revoke access
revokeConfirm.body: {name} loses access to this team at its next token refresh, within 15 minutes.

danger.title: Danger zone
danger.deleteTeamBody: Permanently delete {name} with all its contacts, emails, domains, API keys, templates, broadcasts and members. This cannot be undone.
danger.deleteAccountBody: Permanently delete your account and sign you out everywhere. Teams you are the only owner of must be deleted or handed over first. This cannot be undone.
danger.deleteAccountError: Could not delete the account. Delete or hand over the teams you own, sign in again, and retry.
